column1: Meaning and Necessity of a Constitution

column2: Definition of Constitution: Supreme written law defining relations among citizens and between citizens and government

column3: Trust and Coordination: Builds trust among diverse social groups
Government Structure: Specifies formation of government and distribution of powers
Limits on Power: Restricts government authority and guarantees citizen rights
Aspirations of People: Reflects goals of a just and good society
Racial Classification: Division into White, Black, Coloured, and Indian groups
Political Exclusion: Denial of voting rights to non-whites
Segregation: Separate schools, hospitals, churches, and public spaces
African National Congress: Led resistance against racial discrimination
Nelson Mandela: Imprisoned for 27 years for opposing apartheid
End of Discrimination: Repeal of apartheid laws and political bans
Multi-Racial Government: Democracy established on 26 April 1994
Consensus-Based: Drafted through discussions between oppressors and oppressed
World-Class Document: Guarantees extensive fundamental rights
Partition Violence: Large-scale loss of life during India–Pakistan partition
Integration of States: Unification of princely states
Nehru Report (1928): Early draft of a democratic constitution
Karachi Session (1931): Commitment to fundamental rights and democracy
Democratic Ideals: Universal adult franchise and minority protection
Colonial Laws: Adaptation from Government of India Act, 1935
Global Inspirations

column4: French Revolution: Ideas of liberty and equality

column3: Representative Body: 299 elected members
Election Method: Chosen mainly by Provincial Legislatures
Adoption Date: 26 November 1949
Enforcement Date: 26 January 1950 (Republic Day)
Systematic Process: Open and consensual functioning
Drafting Committee: Chaired by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
Recorded Discussions: Preserved in 12 volumes
Interpretative Value: Explain intent behind constitutional provisions

column2: Philosophical Foundation: Describes aims and ideals of the Constitution
Sovereign: Supreme authority rests with the people
Socialist: Commitment to reduce economic inequality
Secular: Equal respect for all religions
Democratic: Government elected by people with equal political rights
Republic: Head of state is elected, not hereditary

column3: Justice: Social, economic, and political fairness
Liberty: Freedom of thought, expression, and belief
Equality: Equal opportunity and status for all citizens
Fraternity: Sense of unity and brotherhood
Dynamic Constitution: Allows changes with evolving needs
Constitutional Amendments: Legal procedure for updates
Power Distribution: Division of authority among institutions
Limits on Power: Rights act as checks on government authority
